finding: HEADLINE: pam/ is 35.57 GB across 28827 files — .git history is 27.88 GB (78.4%) in only 107 files; the working tree is 7.69 GB. The reported 28 GB is the .git folder. Binary artifacts are 98.1% of the packfile; all C# source is 0.8%
impact: Deleting files today reclaims nothing — the cost is in history

finding: Three third-party ZIP archives are 73.3% of the repository: ARCONDbeaver.zip (50 versions, 11.45 GiB = 41.1% on its own), multitab.zip (48, 4.589 GiB), dbeaver.zip (36, 4.388 GiB). MEASURED PROOF they cannot compress: 44 of 47 versions in the main pack are stored WHOLE with no delta base. Two of the three are DBeaver, an open-source tool that was never ARCON code
basis: git verify-pack -v across both packfiles; delta-base column counted
evidence_command: git verify-pack -v .git/objects/pack/pack-e43e14d9*.idx | aggregate col4 by filename
impact: ARCONDbeaver.zip averages 229 MB of permanent storage per commit of that one file; no redundancy remains for gc or repack to exploit
remediation: Purge with git filter-repo; distribute via artifact store or release page

finding: All .zip content is 80.6% of the main packfile from only 262 file versions — the pattern is broader than the three worst offenders
evidence_command: git verify-pack -v | aggregate col4 by extension
impact: Dominant single cause of repository size
remediation: Purge from history plus a server-side pre-receive hook rejecting archives

finding: Installer packages are committed as source: .msi 1.850 GiB, .exe 1.230 GiB, .deb 0.437 GiB, .pkg 0.211 GiB, .rpm 0.169 GiB on disk. Includes 'ARCON PAM.msi' (7 versions, 0.786 GiB) and dotnetfx.exe, a Microsoft redistributable
evidence_command: git verify-pack -v | aggregate col4 by extension
impact: Installers are build outputs, not source
remediation: Publish to a release/artifact store; purge from history

finding: .gitignore line 363 declares /PAM — the entire product tree — yet 17872 files under PAM/ are tracked. .gitignore never applies to already-tracked files so the rule is inert AND actively misleading. It would also silently block genuinely new PAM/ files from being staged
unit: tracked files under an ignored path
impact: Root cause of continued growth; developers cannot trust the ignore file
remediation: Remove the false /PAM rule; add real artifact rules; git rm --cached the artifacts

finding: 3.69 GiB of the checkout is duplicate filenames at different paths, of which 1.51 GiB is byte-identical. NOTE: git stores identical blobs once, so this is a per-checkout cost not history bloat — but it multiplies history as soon as copies drift and are updated separately
evidence_command: git ls-tree -r -l HEAD | group by basename
impact: Paid by every developer and every CI agent on every clone
remediation: Consolidate to one location and reference rather than copy

finding: msedgedriver.exe is committed at 45 paths with 45 DISTINCT SHAs — 45 genuinely different versions, 593 MB in the checkout alone. chromedriver.exe has 14 copies. Browser drivers are version-pinned downloads, never source
impact: Distinct versions are expensive in BOTH the checkout and history
remediation: Fetch at test time via WebDriverManager or a CI cache

finding: PAM/AllSupportingDLLs is 18.02 GiB of LOGICAL history from only 734 file versions — averaging 25 MB per version. A vendored third-party dependency tree under version control. NOTE: logical size; on-disk will be smaller
evidence_command: aggregate objsizes.txt by top-level area under PAM/
impact: Dependencies should be restorable, not committed
remediation: Migrate to NuGet or an internal package feed

finding: 3326 remote branches and 307 tags. Every ref keeps its blobs reachable so nothing is ever unreachable — this is why git gc reports zero garbage and the pack never shrinks
impact: Blocks all reclamation; makes 'just run gc' useless
remediation: Prune merged and abandoned release branches

finding: Still growing, and one file dominates the growth. A 106-commit pull on 2026-08-10 changing 142 files created a 1.074 GiB pack, of which 0.954 GiB (88.8%) was three NEW versions of ARCONDbeaver.zip — none of which is in HEAD. All C# source in that pull was 0.008 GiB (0.7%)
basis: git verify-pack -v on pack-e625f4b0 (the pull pack), attributed by filename
impact: A routine update transferred ~1 GB of one third-party archive onto branches the developer never checks out
remediation: Fix F04 and F06 first — they are the inflow

finding: No Git LFS and no .gitattributes anywhere in the repository. The standard mitigation for large binaries was never adopted and nothing constrains binary intake
impact: Nothing in the repository prevents the next 370 MB archive from being committed
remediation: Adopt Git LFS (see R03) or add a server-side size-gate hook

finding: A duplicate misnamed 'gitignore' (no leading dot, 6654 bytes) sits beside the real .gitignore (6669 bytes). Git ignores a dotless file entirely; the two differ by 14 lines so rules a developer believes are active are not
impact: Developers trust rules that do nothing
remediation: Delete gitignore after reconciling its 14 differing lines into .gitignore

finding: Media and database binaries in source control: 11 .mp4 (43 MB), 5 .db (111 MB including three ~23 MB SQLite files), 2 .bak (25 MB)
evidence_command: git ls-tree -r -l HEAD | filter by extension
remediation: Move to shared storage; generate test databases at test time

finding: Two junk top-level directories are TRACKED (confirmed, 2 files each): '%LOCALAPPDATA%' — a literal unexpanded environment variable used as a folder name by a script that failed to expand it — and '108.0.5359.125' (a Chrome version) whose chromedriver.exe is a 1-BYTE placeholder file
impact: Evidence of scripted commits reaching main branches without review
remediation: Delete and fix the script that created it

finding: Generated tooling output was committed on some branch: graphify-out/ (1099 file versions, 0.09 GiB) and a 60 MB syftSbomTable.json. NEITHER is in HEAD — both are reachable from other refs, so they still occupy history
remediation: Add to .gitignore; purge in the same history rewrite

finding: COMPARATOR: the entire QA automation repository is 131 MB total — same organisation, same era, comparable team. This repository is 271x larger
impact: Establishes that 35.57 GB is not normal for this organisation

finding: ZERO-RISK, AVAILABLE TODAY: make blobless clone the default for every developer and CI job. Since 98.1% of history is binary blobs almost nobody needs, this avoids nearly all of the 27.88 GB transfer while keeping full history
impact: Removes the developer-side cost without touching server history
remediation: Adopt as the standard clone command

finding: WILL NOT WORK: git gc / git repack reclaim essentially nothing. count-objects reports loose:0 garbage:0 prune-packable:0 and 3326 refs keep everything reachable. More fundamentally 44 of 47 versions of the largest file are ALREADY stored whole because they cannot be delta-compressed — there is no redundancy left to find
basis: git count-objects -vH plus delta-base analysis from git verify-pack -v
impact: Show this output to anyone proposing 'just run gc'

finding: FULL RECLAMATION: purging .zip/.msi/.exe/.deb/.rpm/.pkg from all history targets 26.79 GiB -> ~1.3 GiB, a ~95% reduction. This is arithmetic on measured on-disk pack bytes, not a trial run — only a rehearsal on a clone can confirm it
evidence_command: git filter-repo --strip-blobs-bigger-than 10M (rehearse on a clone first)
impact: Every SHA changes; every clone re-made, every open MR rebased, tags re-signed, pinned CI SHAs updated
remediation: Planned maintenance event with a scheduled freeze
